title: Square up a racked cabinet face frame on the bench until its diagonals match, without sliding it off its marks
instruction: This face frame is out of square. Make it square, with both diagonals the same length, without moving it off the blue corner marks or lifting it, then let go.
context: Assembling cabinet face frames and checking them for square is core work for carpenters (O*NET 47-2031, Core: 'Assemble and fasten materials to make frameworks or props, using hand tools and wood screws, nails, dowel pins, or glue' and 'Verify trueness of structure, using plumb bob and level'; 889,700 US jobs, BLS 2025) and cabinetmakers (51-7011, Core: 'Verify dimensions or check the quality or fit of pieces to ensure adherence to specifications'; 81,800). Frames are dry-assembled and checked for square by the diagonals before glue-up (square when the two corner-to-corner diagonals are equal); if out of square, they are racked along the long diagonal until the diagonals match ('apply clamp pressure across the larger diagonal'). The frame is light, so pushing one corner or dragging one rail only slides it: the hands must work against each other (squeeze the long diagonal, or hold one rail and shift the other). Nothing stops the frame at square: the robot must stop itself within 2 mm.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), heights above the table. Frame: the face frame of an 18 x 12 in wall cabinet, 45.7 cm wide (along y) x 30.5 cm tall (along x), face up and flat on the bare oak bench top (the sim models the station's oak table, friction 0.5, PhysX's default; with the frame's 0.2, PhysX averages poplar on oak to mu 0.35), centred at x 27, y 0; yellow-poplar stock 1.9 cm thick x 3.8 cm wide, 0.47 kg in all. Stiles: 30.5 cm long, along x. Rails: 38.1 cm long between the stiles, along y. Joints: one 5 x 30 mm beech loose tenon (5 x 18.8 x 30 mm) per joint, glued into the rail end and fitted dry, snug in thickness, in a stile mortise 15 mm deep (half the tenon's length) cut at a loose-tenon joiner's middle width setting (6 mm longer than the tenon is wide: 3 mm of play at each end), so each joint turns in the frame's plane; with about 14 mm of tenon engaged in the stile, 0.66 mm of the 3 mm play is used at the 2.7 deg start rack. No glue or clamps in the trial: a dry fit, checked before glue-up. Start: racked 2.7 deg, the far rail 13 mm further left than the near rail, each rail's edge on its pencil mark on the stile; the near-right to far-left diagonal is 20 mm longer than the near-left to far-right one (outer corner to outer corner). Blue tape L-marks on the table 3 mm outside each start corner. Arms start in the ready pose.
scoring: Diagonals measured with a tape, outer corner to outer corner; d = their difference. Latched 0 for the trial if any outer corner ever moves more than 25 mm from its start mark (frame slid or turned off its outline), any part of the frame comes more than 1 cm off the table, or (real rig) a rail is pulled away from its stile (both shoulder corners more than 3 mm off it). Otherwise: 1.0 d <= 2 mm, each rail's edge within 1 mm of its pencil mark on both stiles (shoulder gaps closed <= 0.5 mm), with the frame let go (no robot part within 2.5 cm of it) and still; 0.75 d <= 2 mm, each rail's edge within 1 mm of its pencil mark on both stiles (shoulder gaps closed <= 0.5 mm), but still held or moving; 0.5 d <= 6 mm; 0.25 d <= 12 mm; else 0 (in the sim the pin joints keep the rails on their marks, and d <= 2 mm closes the shoulders to 0.18 mm; start d = 20 mm; racking past square counts the same as falling short). Success when 1.0 holds for 1 s; otherwise scored at the last step. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Rack the frame back by hand to the start (long diagonal 20 +- 1 mm longer, each rail on its pencil mark) and set its corners on the tape marks. Check the joint drag at each reset: hold the near rail down and push the far-left stile 3 cm from its end, along the rails, with a 10 N push-pull gauge; it must start to rack at 1.5-2.5 N. Below that, fit fresh tenons; above it, rub paste wax on the tenon faces. Then check the bench: with nothing held, push the near-right outer corner along the long diagonal (toward the far-left corner) with the same gauge; the whole frame must slide (at about 1.5 N) without racking (the diagonals unchanged within 1 mm). If it racks instead, wipe the bench top clean and dry. Nothing sharp or heavy: no hazards.
fidelity: Full size. Members are rigid boxes; each joint is a pin at its shoulder with Coulomb drag (sim push-gauge check: racks at 2.05 N), frame on table mu 0.35 (wood on wood 0.25-0.5). The loop-closing joint is frictionless; the other three carry its drag. The real mortise also lets a rail slide +-3 mm along its stile; the sim omits that. Sim: one push at a corner slides the frame at 1.53 N; two along the long diagonal rack it at 2.98 N each; no stop at square; spring-back <= 0.43 mm.
